I study how regulatory DNA controls transcription in plants: where transcription
starts, how much of it happens, and how those decisions change during development
and in response to the environment. My work combines genome-wide assays of
transcription initiation and chromatin, plant genetics, and computational models
of regulatory sequence, and I write and maintain open-source software for the
genomics community.

Using csRNA-seq during *Arabidopsis* germination, I showed that plant enhancers can
be transcribed into enhancer RNAs, as in animals
([Nature Communications, 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-46082-5)). I also
wrote and maintain [universalmotif](software.qmd#universalmotif), a toolkit for
sequence motif analysis that has been downloaded more than 150,000 times since 2018.

I am a postdoctoral scientist in
[Tatsuya Nobori's group](https://www.tsl.ac.uk/our-work/scientific-groups/tatsuya-nobori-group)
at The Sainsbury Laboratory in Norwich. I did my PhD with
[Julia Qüesta](https://www.cragenomica.es/research-groups/epigenetics-and-plant-development)
at CRAG in Barcelona and my MSc with
[Barbara Moffatt](https://uwaterloo.ca/biology/profiles/barbara-moffatt) at the
University of Waterloo.

More on my [research](research.qmd), [software](software.qmd) and
[publications](publications.qmd), or see my [CV](cv.qmd).
